claims.text: Pulumi has a provider support policy that specifies how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version, and which providers receive long-term security updates.
Pulumi publishes a provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/.
Pulumi's provider version support policy focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers Pulumi maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page (linked at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/) lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry (at /registry/) lets users find the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
The 'Provider support policy' link at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ points to a page describing Pulumi's provider support policy.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.
For every stack, Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key, which it uses to encrypt secrets for that stack.
Encrypting the same value across two different stacks leads to different encrypted strings being stored in the Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml files, because a different key is used for each stack.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine in any way.
Some Pulumi providers use the open-source Terraform schemas in order to know what resources and parameters are available, and to determine the return and response attributes.
Pulumi native providers are mapped directly to the cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in, requiring explicit enabling via a flag, command, or environment variable such as PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true.
Experimental Pulumi features can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The current list of providers that receive long-term support updates on eligible older versions is: AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Pulumi publishes an AWS provider at /registry/packages/aws/.
Pulumi publishes an Azure Classic provider at /registry/packages/azure/.
Pulumi publishes an Azure Native provider at /registry/packages/azure-native/.
Pulumi publishes an Azure AD provider at /registry/packages/azuread/.
Pulumi publishes a Command provider at /registry/packages/command/.
Pulumi publishes a Docker Build provider at /registry/packages/docker-build/.
Pulumi publishes a GCP provider at /registry/packages/gcp/.
Pulumi publishes a Kubernetes provider at /registry/packages/kubernetes/.
Pulumi publishes a TLS provider at /registry/packages/tls/.
Pulumi publishes a Vault provider at /registry/packages/vault/.

An LTS release for a covered provider ships high/Critical CVE security patches, specifically fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship those CVE fixes.

An LTS release for a covered provider does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or new resource properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility updates with newer versions of language runtimes.
Providers on the LTS branch remain compatible only with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at, unless otherwise prompted via security fixes.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.

When a covered provider's major version N+1 ships, N+1 becomes the new current major (N), the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the previous LTS major reaches end of life on that same day regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within a covered provider's long-term support major version, only the latest minor version receives patches, and earlier minors are frozen.
LTS releases for covered providers are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases, but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a covered provider will automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and this is the recommended approach.
Pinning to a specific major version is the recommended approach for consuming LTS releases.
At any time, exactly one major version of a covered provider is the LTS version, and older major versions receive no patches.

For a covered provider's current major version (N), support lasts until N+1 ships, and it receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions.

For a covered provider's long-term support major version (N−1), support lasts up to 12 months from N's release or until N+1 ships, and it receives only security updates in the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
Provider major versions N−2 and older are end of life, are not supported, and will not receive updates.
There is a page titled "Best practices for maintaining provider versions" at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/#what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions.
There is a Pulumi Registry page at /registry/.
There is a "Getting support" page at /docs/support/getting-support/.
